title: Class Table Inheritance Key Collision (Punning Keys Across Tables)
pattern: Concrete subclass tables in a Class Table Inheritance hierarchy generating their own independent auto-incrementing surrogate keys without a shared sequence registry.
why_bad: Key collisions. If `footballers` and `cricketers` both assign key `101`, any collection or polymorphic join on the parent `players` table will load incorrect rows or cause primary key constraint violations when merging records in memory [328, 645].
detection: Child tables in a class table inheritance structure using independent `AUTO_INCREMENT` or separate database-level sequences for their primary keys.
counterexample: Single table inheritance where all rows share a single primary key sequence.
fix: Use a single parent key generator or share a common sequence across all subclasses to ensure key uniqueness.
